notes: CLOSED 2026-08-30 by a native, axiom-free kernel construction. `AntitoneOn f s := forall a in s, forall b in s, a<=b -> f b <= f a` and `x in Set.Ioi c := c < x` are both Mathlib pointwise `def`s (no kernel `Set` type needed), so with `n` fixed this is the core-rendered unfolding `forall a b, 1<a -> 1<b -> a<=b -> log b n <= log a n` -- the same treatment already given `Nat.log_monotone`/`Nat.choose_mono`, this time over a genuinely NEW induction: `Nat.log_aux_antitone_base` proves monotonicity in the BASE with the value held fixed (materially different from `log_aux_mono`, which fixes the base and varies fuel/value), by induction on the shared fuel (both `log b n`/`log a n` are diagonal at the same `n`). Because `1<a`/`1<b` are hypotheses of the statement rather than case-derived, each side's inner `2<=base` guard is already known true unconditionally. The recursive step compares `logAux b f' (n/b)` against `logAux a f' (n/a)` -- different values at different bases -- by chaining the induction hypothesis (bases at the shared value `n/b`) through `log_aux_mono` at the fixed base `a` (values `n/b<=n/a` from the new infrastructure lemma `Nat.div_le_div_left`, the mirror image of `div_le_div_right`, monotone decreasing in the divisor). `crates/axeyum-lean-kernel/src/nat_prelude/log_clog_order.rs`. This is a genuine library-composition increment, not a found pre-existing declaration.
